title: Hostile coverage: runtime, provider and platform fault boundaries

Deliverable: hostile schedules — poison provider output, truncated and interleaved streams, a provider that never terminates, a runtime whose closure drifts between observation and use, an unresolvable or swapped executable, resource exhaustion at the process boundary, and a race between cancellation and natural exit — each pinning the exact stable reason code AND the answering layer.

CROSS-PLATFORM: `PLATFORM_BOUNDARIES` covers linux/macos/windows. A case that silently skips on the current host generates zero cases and passes while proving nothing. Every platform case must either execute or assert the platform-unsupported refusal arm — never skip.

NOT in scope: transport, integrity/codec, durable store, or scheduler/activation boundaries; host-malicious sandbox claims; closing the completeness ratchet; anything under tests/fault/**.

Owned paths: tests/security/runtime-provider-boundaries.security.ts (this subset is large — split into at most three sibling files under tests/security/ if any would exceed 400 lines).

Verification: `pnpm test:security` — read the OUTPUT count line, not the exit code.
definitionOfDone: Every constant in the runtime-provider subset has at least one BEFORE, one AFTER and one RACE case, with a positive case count asserted per constant so a boundary generating zero cases reddens.

Every refusal pins the exact stable reason code AND the answering layer; where a platform layer and a provider layer can both refuse, the fixture is valid at the platform layer so the provider layer is provably the one that answered.
No platform case SKIPS: on a host where a platform arm cannot execute, the case asserts that platform's stable unsupported refusal instead — asserted for linux, macos and windows arms individually.
A never-terminating provider case is BOUNDED and reaches its stable refusal rather than hanging; the test itself is bounded, because a hang reports no verdict rather than a red one.
No hostile case upgrades a truth class to PROVEN or admits provider output as authority; asserted once across the whole slice.
A mutation removing one closure-drift or stream-integrity check from a covered production boundary turns a NAMED test red, with the drill confirming the red lands on the intended assertion.

`pnpm test:security` runs with its exit code captured separately and prints a count line strictly above the pre-task baseline; the HEAD-minus-merge-base failing-path delta over the owned paths is EMPTY.
taskRails: Consume the roster's `runtime-provider` axis tag as the definitive subset; the roster owns the partition.

Drive the real production boundaries. A mock provider standing in for the process seam proves the mock; test doubles are permitted only for the hostile input and for injected faults the production surface already accepts.
Never skip a platform arm. A skipped case generates nothing and passes while proving nothing; assert the platform-unsupported refusal instead.
Fail closed: unobservable provider or runtime state stays UNKNOWN and never gains authority. Provider output is never parsed into authority.
Preserve foreign work; commit only the explicit owned paths by pathspec. Do not touch tests/fault/**.

implementationPlan.description:
PLATFORM ARMS — and the no-skip rule, which matters more on this axis than anywhere else. `PLATFORM_BOUNDARIES`, `PLATFORM_LAYERS`, `PLATFORM_LINUX_LAYER`, `PLATFORM_MACOS_LAYER` and `WINDOWS_PROCESS_LAYERS` span three operating systems, and this suite runs on one of them.
NO CASE MAY SKIP. A case that quietly skips on the current host generates zero cases and passes while proving nothing — the sweep-generated-nothing defect the project rail names. Every platform arm must either EXECUTE, or assert that platform's stable UNSUPPORTED refusal with its exact code and layer. Assert each of the linux, macos and windows arms individually, and assert a positive executed-case count per arm so an arm that silently produced nothing reddens.
HOSTILE INPUT PER BOUNDARY: a platform observation whose host identity fields are forged or exceed `MAX_PLATFORM_IDENTITY_CHARS`; a fact envelope whose truth class is asserted rather than observed; a boundary name outside `PLATFORM_BOUNDARIES`; for `WINDOWS_PROCESS_LAYERS`, a launch request with sparse or over-long argv, a disallowed environment key, an oversized payload, and a broker frame that is truncated, over-length or carries an unknown opcode — `WINDOWS_PROCESS_CODES` has 22 members covering exactly these, so pin against it rather than inventing expectations.
TWO MEASURED TRAPS on the Windows side. First, `openWindowsProcessBoundary` is SYNCHRONOUS on its refusal path and returns `WindowsProcessBoundary | WindowsProcessUnknown` — a case awaiting a rejected promise will wait forever for a refusal that already returned. Second, its `DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS` is 30 MINUTES; a case that inherits it turns a hung boundary into a half-hour stall rather than a red, and this lane runs `fileParallelism: false`. Pass an explicit bounded timeout, well below `MAX_BOUND_MS` (2**31-1, where `setTimeout` clamps to 1ms).
Also: `recovery-anchor-fs.ts:18` gates directory fsync behind `process.platform !== "win32"`, so do NOT assert POSIX durability side effects in a case that runs on Windows — assert the refusal semantics, which hold everywhere.

implementationPlan.description:
PROVIDER AND LAUNCH ARMS — `CLAUDE_LAUNCH_LAYERS`, `CLAUDE_LAUNCH_SELECTION_LAYER`, `CLAUDE_RENDER_LAYERS`, `CLAUDE_RUNTIME_PIN_LAYER`, `CODEX_RENDER_LAYERS`, `PROVIDER_TELEMETRY_LAYERS`, `PROVIDER_USAGE_LAYERS`, `PROVIDER_RUN_LEDGER_LAYERS`.
THE TRAP THAT WILL OTHERWISE MAKE HALF THESE CASES VACUOUS, measured: `launchClaudeWithTelemetry` returns `ok: true` for a launcher that REFUSED and for a delivery that was NOT ATTEMPTED. Both carry a BLIND handoff whose facts are UNKNOWN and whose `telemetryRefusal` field is populated; the ONLY route to `ok: false` is a malformed run ref (`TELEMETRY_RUN_REF_MALFORMED` at `TELEMETRY_INPUT`). So a hostile case asserting `ok === false` will never fire for launch refusals. Assert on `handoff.telemetryRefusal`, `handoff.terminal` and `handoff.infrastructure`, and pin the two blind shapes (`TELEMETRY_LAUNCH_REFUSED` vs `TELEMETRY_LAUNCH_NOT_ATTEMPTED`) as DISTINCT — collapsing them loses which happened.
FIVE LAYERS CAN ANSWER on the telemetry seam — `PROVIDER_TELEMETRY_LAYERS` = TELEMETRY_INPUT, TELEMETRY_LAUNCH, TELEMETRY_CAPTURE, TELEMETRY_SCHEMA, TELEMETRY_RESULT, and the contract's own comment says a test pinning only the code "would stay green once a different layer started answering first". Build each fixture valid at the earlier layers and name the arranged layer in a comment.
HOSTILE INPUT: poison provider output; a capture that is truncated or whose bytes do not decode to their declared digest; interleaved or out-of-order stream records; a result record claiming a schema the parser does not support; a runtime closure that drifts between observation and use; an unresolvable or swapped executable; a render request carrying argv or environment injection.
MESSAGE HYGIENE IS A PRODUCTION RULE AND A TEST RULE. `PROVIDER_TELEMETRY_MESSAGES` are deliberately static and non-interpolating because "a message quoting the captured bytes, the model or a digest would echo provider output back out of a failure path". Assert as a PROPERTY over this file's refusals that no message contains a path, argv, environment value, digest or captured byte — and do not let a test print provider output to demonstrate rejection.
implementationPlan.note:
PROVIDER AND LAUNCH ARMS LANDED — 7 boundaries, 30 cases in this slice; both slices together `Test Files 2 passed (2)` / `Tests 54 passed (54)`, EXIT=0.

THE ok:true TRAP IS DRIVEN, NOT DESCRIBED. `launchClaudeWithTelemetry({providerRunRef: GOOD_REF, request: null})` runs the REAL seam on this win32 host: it returns `ok: true`, and the case asserts `handoff.terminal === "REFUSED"`, `handoff.infrastructure === "LAUNCH_REFUSED"`, `handoff.sequence.known === false`, and pins `handoff.telemetryRefusal` to TELEMETRY_LAUNCH_REFUSED @ TELEMETRY_LAUNCH. A sibling case pins the ONE route to `ok: false` — TELEMETRY_RUN_REF_MALFORMED @ TELEMETRY_INPUT — and a third asserts the two blind codes are DISTINCT members of PROVIDER_TELEMETRY_CODES with different static messages. Nothing in the file branches on `ok` to decide whether something was refused.

FIVE-LAYER DISAMBIGUATION, measured rather than guessed. My first stream fixtures were vacuous: every one refused TELEMETRY_STREAM_ANOMALOUS @ TELEMETRY_SCHEMA because records without `seq` are MALFORMED_RECORD anomalies and records without `schemaVersion: "claude-stream-json/1"` are UNKNOWN_SCHEMA_VERSION. A standalone probe against the compiled parser established the real behaviour, and the fixtures now carry both fields so the deeper layers are reachable. The result:
- TELEMETRY_CAPTURE_UNDECODABLE / _TRUNCATED / _INCOMPLETE @ TELEMETRY_CAPTURE, each from a coherent capture with exactly ONE field flipped.
- TELEMETRY_STREAM_ANOMALOUS @ TELEMETRY_SCHEMA for out-of-order and for resume-discontinuity, and TELEMETRY_SCHEMA_UNSUPPORTED @ TELEMETRY_SCHEMA for an unaccepted schema — same layer, DISTINCT codes, pinned separately.
- TELEMETRY_MODEL_AMBIGUOUS @ TELEMETRY_RESULT off a stream that PARSES. That case is the strongest in the file: two admitted init records naming different models, the parse succeeds, and the model fact stays UNKNOWN rather than one record becoming authority.
- TELEMETRY_RUN_REF_MALFORMED @ TELEMETRY_INPUT, arranged with a coherent capture so no later layer can answer.

MESSAGE HYGIENE is asserted as a PROPERTY over the whole refusal set (paths, hex digests, base64 blobs, secret-shaped env values, and the literal hostile inputs), not one example. No test prints provider output; the hygiene helper deliberately does not quote offending bytes.

HONEST CORRECTION recorded rather than papered over: `claudeFailure`/`codexFailure` return `{ok, code, message}` with NO layer — the render layer vocabulary lives on the ACCEPTED envelope's manifest. My first draft asserted a hand-built `{code, layer}` against itself, which is a tautology. Replaced by two recorders: `refusedWithoutLayer` asserts the code against production AND asserts the surface reports no layer (so a layer that starts being reported reddens), and `refusedByManifestLayer` builds the actual from `entry.exclusionReason` + `entry.layer` read off the production manifest, checked against a hand-written expectation. Same fix applied to the launcher and provider-run blocks, which had been reading a code off production and asserting it against itself.

CLAUDE_LAUNCH_LAYERS: measured that both a throwing accessor and a bare Proxy answer CLAUDE_LAUNCH_REQUEST_MALFORMED @ LAUNCHER — reaching HOSTILE_LAUNCH_OPERAND needs an otherwise-valid request. The case now pins LAUNCHER truthfully, adds a containment assertion that the trap accessor NEVER FIRED, and states that the other members of this composed vocabulary are separate roster entries with their own blocks.

CLAUDE_LAUNCH_SELECTION_LAYER: CLAUDE_LAUNCH_SESSION_RESUMED, CLAUDE_LAUNCH_MODEL_UNPROVEN, CLAUDE_LAUNCH_MODEL_MISMATCH, CLAUDE_LAUNCH_EFFORT_UNPROVEN and CLAUDE_LAUNCH_SELECTION_MALFORMED, each from a selection valid at the arms above the one under test (the resume arm sits ahead of both, so the model-arm case is provably not answered by it).

FILES, all under the 400-line rail by `grep -c ''`: runtime-provider-launch.security.ts 399, runtime-provider-launch-fixtures.ts 240, runtime-provider-render-cases.ts 118, runtime-provider-ledger.ts 283, runtime-provider-platform.security.ts 398, runtime-provider-platform-fixtures.ts 186. The two render boundaries are registered from ONE parameterised builder — their case structure is identical and a copy would let them drift; the codex arm stays provably its own because every code and its layer constant are supplied from that renderer's own exported vocabulary.

implementationPlan.description:
EVIDENCE, WORKSPACE AND SUPERVISION ARMS — `ARTIFACT_ENUMERATION_LAYERS`, `EVIDENCE_REFUSAL_LAYERS`, `VERIFIER_PROCESS_LAYERS`, `MATERIALIZATION_REFUSAL_LAYERS`, `SCOPE_OBSERVER_LAYERS`, `SUPERVISOR_LAYERS`, `RECOVERY_LAYERS`, `RECOVERY_INVENTORY_LAYERS`, `RUNNER_WORKSPACE_LAYER`.
HOSTILE INPUT: an artifact enumeration whose descriptor digest does not match its bytes; a declared artifact ref pointing outside the workspace root, through a symlink, or at a reparse point; an evidence receipt resealed for a different subject; a verifier process that never terminates, exits by signal, or writes more than its bound; a materialization request naming a path that escapes containment; a scope observation claiming authored paths the run never touched; a supervisor effect presented after its grant was consumed.
CONTAINMENT ESCAPES ARE THE HEART OF THIS GROUP. For every path-shaped input, cover the escape family properly: `..` traversal, an absolute path, a symlink whose target is outside, a reparse point, a path that is inside by string comparison but outside after canonicalisation, and one containing a NUL. Pin each with the exact code and layer. Note the macOS `$TMPDIR` symlink (`/var` → `/private/var`) reads as an escape under naive comparison, so a case built on a temp root must canonicalise before asserting — otherwise it passes for the wrong reason on one platform and fails on another.
A NEVER-TERMINATING VERIFIER MUST REACH ITS STABLE REFUSAL, not hang. Bound it explicitly and assert it terminates; a hang reports no verdict at all, and `fileParallelism: false` means it stalls every file after it.
WHOLE-SLICE INVARIANT, asserted once over the collected outcomes across all three files rather than per case: no hostile input yields an admitted artifact, an accepted evidence receipt, a materialized path outside containment, an executed effect, or a truth class above UNKNOWN. Provider output is never parsed into authority.
COMPLETENESS: assert a positive case count per boundary, and assert the union of the three files' swept boundaries equals the roster's 22 runtime-provider entries in BOTH directions.
implementationPlan.note:
EVIDENCE, WORKSPACE AND SUPERVISION ARMS LANDED. All three slices green: `Test Files 3 passed (3)` / `Tests 86 passed (86)`, EXIT=0, lane tsc clean on my files.

NINE BOUNDARIES, each with BEFORE/AFTER/RACE and a positive per-arm count:
- ARTIFACT_ENUMERATION_LAYERS — RUNNER_ARTIFACT_ENUMERATION_UNAVAILABLE @ ARTIFACT_STORE vs RUNNER_ARTIFACT_VERIFY_FAILED / _MISSING @ ARTIFACT_FS_PORT. The two layers are pinned APART, and one case proves the capability gate answers FIRST even when the directory is also absent.
- EVIDENCE_REFUSAL_LAYERS — RUNNER_EVIDENCE_ARTIFACT_REF_INVALID and RUNNER_EVIDENCE_ARGV_INVALID, both @ RECIPE_SHAPE, pinned separately so neither can answer for the other.
- VERIFIER_PROCESS_LAYERS — VERIFIER_PROCESS_RECIPE_SEAL_INVALID @ LAUNCH_GATE with an injected launcher that RECORDS then THROWS: `expect(spawns).toEqual([])` proves zero children, and the RACE case asserts BOTH legs settled, which is what a hang would deny.
- MATERIALIZATION_REFUSAL_LAYERS — RUNNER_MATERIALIZATION_SELECTION_INVALID @ SEAL vs RUNNER_MATERIALIZATION_MANIFEST_TAMPERED @ STALENESS, raced against each other so each answers at its own layer.
- SCOPE_OBSERVER_LAYERS — GIT_OBSERVER via `classifyRefFailure`, plus the escape family via `observeScope`.
- SUPERVISOR_LAYERS — EFFECT_INTENT_MALFORMED and EFFECT_GRANT_MALFORMED @ KERNEL; the AFTER case presents a consumed grant TWICE and is refused twice, so replay confers nothing.
- RECOVERY_LAYERS — RECOVERY_BOUNDARY_MALFORMED @ SAFE_BOUNDARY vs RECOVERY_OBSERVATION_MALFORMED @ CLASSIFICATION.
- RECOVERY_INVENTORY_LAYERS — RECOVERY_INVENTORY_REQUEST_INVALID @ INVENTORY_ADAPTER, asserting `items` is undefined so nothing was partially collected.
- RUNNER_WORKSPACE_LAYER — RUNNER_WORKSPACE_INPUT_MANIFEST_INVALID from `buildResultManifest`.

CONTAINMENT: a hand-written nine-member ESCAPE_FAMILY (dot-dot, embedded traversal, single dot, posix absolute, drive-qualified, backslash, reserved device, trailing space, embedded NUL) swept by three boundaries. Each sweep asserts a POSITIVE member count FIRST, and the scope sweep additionally asserts more than one DISTINCT code came back — a single catch-all would prove nothing about which reinterpretation was caught. The symlink case builds a real link under a realpath'd `withHostileRoot` and asserts containment AFTER canonicalisation, with a positive control (`inside.txt` IS contained); where Windows refuses symlink creation it does NOT skip but asserts the same containment rule on the canonical target.

TWO HONEST NARROWINGS, both asserted rather than assumed:
1. `scopeFailure` and `buildResultManifest` report a code and NO layer by production design. `refusedWithoutLayer` asserts the code against production AND asserts the absence of a layer, so a layer that starts being reported reddens and forces the case to pin it. SCOPE_OBSERVER_LAYERS still carries a layer-attributed case via `classifyRefFailure`, so its one declared layer is exercised.
2. planningNotes.risks:
1) THE `ok: true` TRAP would hollow out the provider group silently — every launch-refusal case would pass without firing. Drill 1 is the guard; if it stays green those cases branched on `ok` and tested nothing.

2) A SKIPPED PLATFORM ARM generates zero cases and passes. Three OSes, one host. Assert the UNSUPPORTED refusal instead, with per-arm positive counts.

3) FIVE LAYERS ANSWER ON THE TELEMETRY SEAM. A code-only assertion detaches the moment a different one answers first — the contract says so itself. Build fixtures valid at the earlier layers and name the arranged layer per case.

4) MESSAGE HYGIENE IS A REJECTION HISTORY, not a style note. Assert it as a property over the whole refusal set; one example would not have caught the original defect either.

5) A CONTAINMENT CASE CAN PASS FOR THE WRONG REASON. macOS `$TMPDIR` symlinks read as escapes; a missing file and an escape both refuse. Canonicalise, and require drill 3's red to land on the escape.

6) A HANGING VERIFIER OR AN UNBOUNDED WINDOWS CASE reports no verdict and stalls the whole lane under `fileParallelism: false`. Explicit bounds well below `MAX_BOUND_MS` (2**31-1, where `setTimeout` clamps to 1ms).

7) AWAITING A SYNCHRONOUS REFUSAL. `openWindowsProcessBoundary` returns its refusal rather than rejecting; a case awaiting a promise waits for something that already happened.
